chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the marriage of a Jewish woman and a Christian woman, so he said, 'There is no objection.' I said, 'And a Magian woman?' He said, 'There is no objection with her,' meaning temporary marriage.

key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on marrying Jewish, Christian, and Magian women?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of marrying Jewish, Christian, and Magian women, extending the traditional categories of 'People of the Book' to include Zoroastrians, who were widely regarded as such in Shia jurisprudence. Notably, he specifies that the ruling for the Magian woman applies specifically to temporary marriage (mut'ah), highlighting a nuanced distinction in marital contracts within the Shia legal tradition. This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh regarding interfaith marriage, particularly in the context of mut'ah, which is less commonly discussed in Sunni jurisprudence.
